teams.heading: Jake White eyes trusted Springbok ally for Fiji coaching team
teams.body: Jake White's assistant coaches remain unannounced. Reports have the former Springboks boss eyeing a trusted Springbok ally for his Fiji coaching team, after Fiji appointed him head coach in mid-October ahead of the 2027 World Cup. No announcement of those assistant coaches appears in today's coverage, and the ally is still not named in the reports.

teams.heading: RFU extends Steve Borthwick's contract to 2028, backing him through autumn results
teams.body: Bill Sweeney, the RFU chief executive, has extended Steve Borthwick's contract by six months to mid-2028 and cannot envisage him being out of post for next year's World Cup in Australia, whatever the autumn results. The move comes despite England's worst Six Nations performance under Borthwick earlier this year, which Sweeney said he was very disappointed by. "We believe in what he's doing," Sweeney said. He wants to see continued progress, and the RFU is backing Borthwick to deliver it.

lead.why: It is a new, concrete event: the RFU has extended Borthwick's contract and its chief executive has said he will not be removed before the World Cup.

teams.heading: Clermont sign All Blacks prop Ofa Tu'ungafasi for three months' injury cover
teams.body: Clermont have signed All Blacks prop Ofa Tu'ungafasi on a three-month injury-cover deal, announced on Tuesday. The 34-year-old can play either prop position and played the last of his 68 Tests in November 2024. Clermont head coach Christophe Urios said: "This is a fantastic opportunity that we've seized." Scrum anchor Régis Montagne will be away with France this month, and Clermont are missing Cristian Ojovan and Sacha Lotrian.

lead.why: Item 1 is women's rugby (Trailfinders Women), items 4 and 5 were already run, and item 2 is an Italy U20 squad, so this is the freshest men's France-linked item left.

teams.heading: Andy Farrell hands Nick Timoney and Craig Casey starts against Argentina
teams.body: Timoney starts at openside and Casey at scrum-half for the Nations Championship clash with Argentina at the Aviva Stadium, Dublin, and Sam Prendergast is fit to start at fly-half after the wrist injury that had him in doubt. Andrew Porter, Ryan Baird and Mack Hansen all return from injuries that kept them out of the green jersey for a year. Sean Jansen wins only his second Test start, at number eight, with Caelan Doris and Jack Conan absent, and Garry Ringrose is sidelined.

lead.why: A fresh Ireland selection event with a named, numbered lineup, which is the squad news a fan would act on.

teams.heading: Muhamed Hasa braces Italy for scrum battle with Springboks' front row
teams.body: Italy prop Muhamed Hasa says the scrum will be one of the key aspects of Saturday's Nations Championship Test in Turin, and he will face a Springboks front row featuring Ox Nché, Malcolm Marx and Thomas du Toit. "South Africa are arguably the best team in the world in that area," the Zebre prop said at a media briefing. Italy are without captain Michele Lamaro, centres Ignacio Brex and Tommaso Menoncello and winger Louis Lynagh, and Hasa admitted the absences create an opportunity for others to step up.

lead.why: A fresh, Italy-side item with a sourced quote from Italy's prop on the scrum, the match's key battle, which the reader hasn't seen before.

teams.heading: Freddy Douglas and Ollie Blyth-Lafferty called up late for All Blacks test
teams.body: Late additions Freddy Douglas and Ollie Blyth-Lafferty give Gregor Townsend more options before Saturday's test against the All Blacks, but the BBC's Tom English is more interested in who has been left out. English says Townsend clearly believes he already has enough carriers, calls Magnus Bradbury's omission harsh and suggests the coach does not trust him. Townsend had initially left Douglas out because of cover at seven, a call a reader asked English to revisit.

lead.why: It is the only fresh squad item in the pack, covering late call-ups for Saturday's New Zealand test.

teams.heading: Ronan O'Gara says Wales' coaching ticket delivers progress; Japan win non-negotiable
teams.body: Former Ireland fly-half and ITV pundit Ronan O'Gara believes Steve Tandy's coaching team is making progress, and that Wales should be judged on it. “Wins for Wales aren’t measured by victories now,” he said. Beating Japan this month is, in his view, non-negotiable. He argues that 14 of Tandy's 39-man squad playing in the Prem could rebuild the winning habit Wales have lacked at Test level.

lead.why: O'Gara's verdict on Tandy's coaching team is the strongest new Wales item in the pack with a direct quote and a clear stake for Wales ahead of the Japan match.

teams.heading: Contepomi makes twelve changes to Pumas side for Dublin, Mallía back
teams.body: Only Boris Wenger, Guido Petti and Pablo Matera survive from the XV that drew 28-28 with Australia in September, for Friday's Nations Championship match at the Aviva Stadium. The headline return is fullback Juan Cruz Mallía, back for the first time in almost a year after ruptured knee ligaments from a late tackle by England's Tom Curry. Argentina have never beaten Ireland away from home in 11 meetings, and Contepomi calls Friday "a massive, massive challenge" one year out from the World Cup.

lead.why: A fresh selection event with the biggest squad consequences: Contepomi's near-complete reshuffle and Mallía's return ahead of Friday's Test.

teams.heading: Kurtley Beale, 37, recalled to Wallabies squad for northern hemisphere Nations tour
teams.body: Les Kiss has named Beale for the northern leg, which takes in England, Scotland and Wales, replacing Hunter Paisami, unavailable for personal reasons. Beale, who turns 38 in January, last played a Test in 2021, against Wales in Cardiff, and an Achilles injury cut short his last squad stint in 2024. He says his role now is to "create some competition within the team", and he has been with the Western Force since 2024.

lead.why: A fresh squad selection with named veteran Kurtley Beale is a new Australia event, and it is not the already-read Schmidt or England-injury stories.

teams.heading: Japan face sold-out Principality lower tier as Wales release extra tickets
teams.body: Japan's visit to Cardiff is shaping up as a big occasion: the Welsh Rugby Union says the lower tier at the Principality Stadium has sold out for the Nations Championship fixture, prompting extra under-18 tickets in the middle and upper tiers. Adults pay from £31, students £22 and under-18s £16. The WRU also expects thousands of supporters in Cardiff, with a free Fan Zone Cymru at Cardiff Arms Park.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item on the shortlist, and it gives Japan's Cardiff trip a concrete fact about the crowd they will face.

teams.heading: Mike Blair says Barrett and McKenzie are 'really key to our attacks'
teams.body: Attack coach Mike Blair has singled out Beauden Barrett and Damian McKenzie ahead of Saturday's Murrayfield Test. Their ability to switch in and out of first receiver and play-make from different areas is "really key to our attacks," Blair said. Ruben Love wore 10 in all three July Nations Championship Tests, with McKenzie at full-back and Barrett out of the matchday squad. Injuries to Love and Richie Mo'unga then moved McKenzie to fly-half for the two Bledisloe Cup Tests, both comfortable All Blacks wins.

lead.why: It is the only NEW shortlist item, and it carries an on-record coach's assessment of New Zealand's playmaking before Saturday's Test.

teams.heading: Jasper Wiese says Springboks won't underestimate Italy after Perth defeat
teams.body: Wiese, who earned his 50th Test cap in Perth, will start again on Saturday when the Boks face Italy in Turin. Asked about complacency, the No 8 told the media on Wednesday: "We don't want to become complacent and then lose." He pointed to the 38-42 defeat to Australia, played with an understrength side, and said a couple of things went against the team there. Erasmus has picked his strongest available side, while Italy are without 16 injured players, including captain Michele Lamaro.

lead.why: A new, South Africa-angled item with concrete facts: Wiese's comments on complacency, his 50th cap and the Perth defeat.
